text: In network analysis of biological systems, a scale-free network's degree distribution follows which mathematical form?
choices: P(k) ~ k^(-γ), a power-law distribution with a few high-degree hubs
P(k) ~ e^(-k/k₀), an exponential distribution with a capped maximum degree
P(k) ~ N(μ,σ²), a Gaussian distribution centered on the mean degree
P(k) = 1/N for all k, a uniform distribution across degrees
explanation: Scale-free biological networks (e.g., many PPI networks) follow a power-law degree distribution P(k)~k^(-γ), producing a small number of highly connected hub nodes and many low-degree nodes. Exponential distributions (second option) describe networks with a capped degree such as the E. coli regulatory network, not scale-free ones. Gaussian and uniform distributions (third and fourth options) would produce a typical degree with no hubs, contradicting the hub-dominated topology seen in many biological networks.
